title: The polynomial $X^Q-X$ has only simple roots in characteristic $p$
statement: Let $p$ be a prime, let $L$ be a field of characteristic $p$, and let $Q$ be an integer divisible by $p$. Then every root of the polynomial $f=X^Q-X\in L[X]$ in $L$ [def-weil-polynomial-root] is a simple root: $(X-\alpha)^2$ does not divide $f$ for any $\alpha\in L$; equivalently, in the multiset of roots of $f$ in $L$ no element occurs twice. (Reason: $f$ is separable, since its derivative is $f'=QX^{Q-1}-1=-1$, so $f$ and $f'$ are coprime.)

source.place: Lang, Algebra, Ch. V, §5, proof of Theorem 5.1 (the derivative of $X^{q^n}-X$ is $-1$, so the roots are distinct); the document is wanted, not obtained: statement written by an agent
